data.title: Fed rate hike odds: FedWatch vs. prediction markets
data.description:
Markets are pricing in another interest rate hike in the Federal Reserve's policy meeting next month as inflation remains stubbornly high and the labor market is stable.

Last week, the Federal Open Market Committee raised its benchmark lending rate by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4%. And 16 policymakers see one more hike this year, while two see rates holding steady.

The odds of a 25-basis-point hike in October neared 70%, according to CME's FedWatch tool at the time of writing. That's up from 58% a week ago and ~10% in the prior month.

Meanwhile, on Kalshi (KALSHI), the chances of an October hike stood at 67%, up from ~50% last week and 22% a month ago. On Polymarket (POLYMARKET), the odds of a 25-bp hike were at 65%.

It's interesting that prediction markets, which show binary event contracts, tend to line up with expectations derived from Fed Funds futures.

Platforms like Kalshi (KALSHI) and Polymarket (POLYMARKET) reflect bets from individual speculators and retail traders. On the other hand, FedWatch acts as a barometer for institutional expectations of the Fed Funds target rate.

A recent working paper in the Finance and Economics Discussion Series (FEDS) found that prediction markets can complement existing forecast tools in both research and policy settings. 

"By providing transparent, continuously updated and economically interpretable measures of expectations with competitive forecast performance, they open new avenues for studying monetary policy transmission, market sentiment, and macroeconomic uncertainty," the working paper stated. 

Moreover, retail traders' accessibility to prediction markets offers a perspective on the Fed rate outlook that's distinct from institutionally dominated markets.

Prediction markets have grown in popularity over the past year. According to The Block, Kalshi's (KALSHI) cumulative monthly volume has reached $244.6B so far.

Polymarket's (POLYMARKET) cumulative monthly volume is at $110.16B as of Friday. Polymarket U.S., which launched in Dec. 2025, now has a cumulative monthly volume of $22.34B.

But FedWatch is underpinned by the more established Fed Funds futures market, which trades ~$2.8T notional average daily volume.

Even so, as prediction markets mature and liquidity deepens over time, their potential to enhance real-time policy analysis will only grow, according to the FEDS working paper.

data.title: Homebuilding stocks showing oversold signals as sector faces further pressure
data.description:
Homebuilding stocks have faced sustained selling pressure this year, and Pantheon Economics said there is “no relief in sight” for homebuilders’ stock prices as higher mortgage rates, weakening affordability and elevated inventories weigh on the sector.

Against this backdrop, a screen of homebuilding stocks based on their Relative Strength Index identifies 11 names with the lowest readings, suggesting they have experienced comparatively strong selling pressure. Installed Building Products (IBP) tops the list with an RSI of 34, followed by Dream Finders Homes (DFH) at 35 and KB Home (KBH) at 37.

The broader weakness in homebuilders has been significant. Pantheon Economics noted that the Dow Jones US Select Home Construction Total Return Index underperformed the S&P 500 Total Return Index by 23 percentage points in both 2024 and 2025.

That relative weakness has continued this year, with the homebuilders index down 5% on a total-return basis compared with a 14% gain for the S&P 500.

The latest RSI screen includes several of the sector's publicly traded builders, with Smith Douglas Homes (SDHC) and M/I Homes (MHO) posting RSI readings of 37 and 38, respectively. LGI Homes (LGIH) and Hovnanian Enterprises (HOV) each have an RSI of 40, while Boxabl (BXBL) stands at 41.

Pantheon Economics said recent new-home sales data offers limited evidence of improvement. July sales were revised up to 643,000 from 607,000 previously, while August sales were preliminarily estimated at 684,000, an eight-month high.

However, the firm cautioned that the August estimate has a 90% confidence interval of ±20 percentage points around the reported 6.4% increase, meaning the underlying trend could be closer to flat and remains subdued.

Meanwhile, the NAHB survey’s expected single-family home sales index fell to 37 in September from 43 in August, its lowest level since January 2023, suggesting builders are anticipating weaker demand ahead. PulteGroup (PHM), Meritage Homes (MTH) and Toll Brothers (TOL) round out the screen, with RSI readings of 42, 43 and 43, respectively.

The housing backdrop could create additional pressure on builders’ margins. Pantheon Economics expects new-home sales to weaken as renewed increases in mortgage rates weigh on affordability.

Homebuilders have already been cutting prices to support sales, with the median price of a new single-family home down 2.6% year-over-year in the three months through August. At the current pace of sales, it would take about 8.5 months to clear existing unsold inventory, compared with a 60-year average of six months.

The RSI is a momentum oscillator that ranges from 0 to 100, with readings below 30 generally considered oversold and readings above 70 viewed as overbought. While none of the stocks in the screen has fallen below 30, their relatively low readings point to notable recent selling pressure as the sector faces the prospect of weaker sales and further margin compression.

data.title: Apple's new HomePod mini 2 to come in new variants: report
data.description:
• Apple (AAPL) hasn't released an updated version of the HomePod mini in a few years, but a new version of the smart speaker is expected to be released this year and come in new colors, MacRumors reported.
  • The updated HomePod mini, which is expected to incorporate Apple Intelligence and potentially Siri AI, will come in blue, black, green, pink, and white, the news outlet added, citing source code from Apple.   • Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Seeking Alpha.

data.title: U.S. natural gas futures pull back after biggest drop in nearly three months
data.description:
U.S. natural gas futures turned lower Friday, reversing some of the previous session's big gains that were largely due to an interruption on TC Energy's (TRP) Columbia Gas Transmission pipeline in West Virginia that affected as much as 1.5% of total U.S. Lower-48 gas supply.

The leak triggered a force majeure and subsequent capacity reduction on the Mountaineer Xpress pipeline in West Virginia, cutting firm transportation service through the key conduit by 1.8 Bcf/day and causing prices to shoot up on Thursday.

The shutdown compounded production losses in recent weeks as producers in Appalachia reduced output ahead of the lower-demand autumn shoulder season.

"It now appears that this outage could prove brief," Ritterbusch & Associates said in a note. "Yesterday's price response to the pipeline outage was likely exacerbated by a continued heavy speculative presence on the short side of this market, where participants have likely been lulled to sleep by what has been a sizable storage cushion across the past summer."

U.S. front-month Nymex October natural gas (NG1:COM) fell 5.5% so far on Friday to $3.115/MMBtu, after surging 9% on Thursday to its highest settlement since June 25.

In Europe, natural gas prices are on track for a more than 5% weekly loss amid hopes for diplomatic progress toward ending the Middle East war and mild seasonal temperatures that continue to delay heating demand.

Still, European Union storage levels are only ~70% full, leaving the market highly sensitive to potential disruptions.

"Unlike oil, LNG flows are more constrained because they depend on specialized tankers and face greater exposure to security risks," ANZ analysts said in a note. "The market has tightened further as Norwegian piped flows to the continent have declined amid maintenance at gas facilities."

data.title: Pershing Square Holdings unveils additional $100M stock buyback program
data.description:
Pershing Square Holdings (PSHZF), Bill Ackman's closed-end fund listed on the London Stock Exchange, is authorized to repurchase up to $100M of additional stock under a new buyback program, the fund said on Friday.

The program is expected to increase its net asset value per share and will reduce the fund's capital. Pershing Square Holdings (PSHZF) stock rose 1.7% in Friday morning trading in New York. Shares repurchased will be held in its Treasury.

Since Pershing Square Holdings started its first share buyback in May 2017, it has repurchased 76.8M  of its public shares for a total of $2.0B at an average price of $25.66. 

The shares recently traded at $48.50.

data.title: Goldman’s guide to the AI valuation reset
data.description:
Although investors remain skeptical about the sustainability of artificial intelligence (AIQ) (AIEQ) earnings growth, equity markets (SPY) (QQQ) have already partially priced in these concerns through sharp valuation de-ratings across AI infrastructure stocks, according to new research from Goldman Sachs.

The median AI infrastructure stock has de-rated from 32x consensus forward earnings in April to 22x today, Goldman wrote in a note to clients published earlier this week. When comparing recent changes in market cap to recent changes in earnings—a signal of how long markets expect current earnings strength to persist—expectations appear most elevated among optical networking, electrical grid and liquid cooling stocks, while outlooks remain most conservative among semiconductors (SMH) (SOXX) and utilities (XLU).

Semiconductor valuations embed particularly skeptical views about earnings durability. Memory stocks (DRAM) trade at a 2-year forward price-to-earnings ratio of just 4x, half their 15-year average, despite enjoying gross margins of roughly 80%—more than double historical norms.

For memory stock P/Es to return to their 15-year average, earnings would need to decline by approximately 50%. Fabless chip stocks present a more compelling opportunity: their margins sit only modestly above historical averages, and earnings would need to decline just 10% to bring valuations back to normal levels, according to Goldman, which maintained Buy ratings on Nvidia (NVDA) and Broadcom (AVGO) while ranking Micron Technology (MU) as Neutral.

Hyperscaler (AMZN) (META) (MSFT) (GOOG) (GOOGL) (ORCL) valuations have de-rated to their lowest levels in over a decade, now trading just four turns above the median S&P 500 (SPY) (VOO) company—the smallest premium on record, the note said. The combination of decelerating capex growth and improving free cash flow visibility should serve as positive catalysts for these stocks.

 

 

Goldman noted that U.S. hyperscalers are on track to spend $800B in capex this year, with consensus expecting $1.1T in 2027—investment levels as a share of GDP not seen since the railroad build-out of the late 1800s. Goldman estimates hyperscalers need some $300B in annual AI revenues to break even on their 2026-2027 capex investments.

While current estimated AI revenues remain below that threshold, cloud revenues have accelerated sharply, with combined backlogs from major providers exceeding $1.7T. 

The application layer would need to generate roughly $1T in annual revenues for hyperscalers to earn solid returns—a figure comparable to the $1.5T in global software spending in 2026 and the $1.8T in potential U.S. labor productivity gains economists estimate will eventually accrue to capital.

data.title: Tamboran outlines at least 6 step-out wells over 18 months as first gas sales enter commissioning
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Tamboran Resources Corporation (TBN) Q4 fiscal 2026

Management View

  • “The last few months have been a pivotal period for Tamboran and the Betaloo Basin” with “First Gas Sales from the Betaloo to the Northern Territory Gas market,” CEO Todd Abbott said (Chief Executive Officer Todd Abbott).

  • Abbott framed near-term revenue mechanics around commissioning and contract terms: “Gas has now been flowing into the market for 20 days,” volumes are “limited by market demand” with the Northern Territory Government “nominating 25 terajoule per day,” and once in supply period “take-or-pay provisions will apply to the 40-terajoule per day contract quantity,” he said (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • On execution and potential cost reductions, Abbott highlighted scale and early efficiency signals: “We completed 178 stages across 30,000 lateral feet,” achieved “Betaloo Basin record 12 stages completed in a day,” and said in-basin sand “could save USD 4 million per well with a 10,000-foot horizontal section,” while the Sturt Plateau compression facility was completed “on time and approximately USD 9 million below the forecasted budget” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • Balance sheet and accounting timing were central to the update: “In April, we raised USD 186 million net of fees,” and “at the end of the quarter, Tamboran had USD 225 million in cash and USD 31 million in undrawn debt,” Abbott said, adding that “over the next 2 quarters… some revenue and costs related to the Pilot Project will be capitalized to the balance sheet during commissioning,” and “we expect to announce first quarterly gas sales and revenue in our 1Q fiscal '27 earnings in November” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • CFO Eric Dyer emphasized early appraisal learnings and capital discipline on the Eastern depocenter history: “There was a vertical frac done by Santos… 2019 that hit most of the zones,” but “really, that's all off of one vertical frac from 7 years ago,” and “capital is precious, and we've got to be very careful with what we're doing” (Chief Financial Officer Eric Dyer).

Outlook

  • Tamboran described a transition from commissioning pricing to contracted volumes: “During the commissioning period, we will be receiving 75% of the gas price,” and “once commissioning and production testing requirements are complete, we will commence delivery into the take-or-pay contract with the Northern Territory Government,” Abbott said (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • Management tied near-term production history to nomination ramps rather than well constraints: “The 25 terajoules a day is a Northern Territory Government limitation,” and Abbott said, “probably by the end of the year, we'll see… that 40 terajoule a day target,” while also noting seasonality may reduce nominations again “later, as we go into next year” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • On the next development phase and partnering, Abbott said the company plans “to drill and stimulate at least 6 step-out wells over the next 18 months” with joint-venture partners and is “progressing discussions with multiple parties to bring in a strategic partner,” with the capital program “not… fully locked-in until we finalize who our partner is” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

Financial Results

  • The transcript did not include quarterly revenue, EPS, or margin figures; Abbott instead highlighted liquidity and commissioning accounting. He said, “at the end of the quarter, Tamboran had USD 225 million in cash and USD 31 million in undrawn debt,” and “including the USD 15 million that we expect to receive from Daly Waters Energy, the pro forma cash position is USD 240 million,” while noting the $15 million receipt “remains subject to certain conditions precedent” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • Abbott also described a near-term reporting impact: “Over the next 2 quarters… some revenue and costs related to the Pilot Project will be capitalized to the balance sheet during commissioning, rather than flowing through the income statement,” and said this “means that the income statement will not reflect cash movements during the period” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • On capital efficiency, Abbott cited project execution: “construction of the Sturt Plateau compression facility” was completed “approximately USD 9 million below the forecasted budget,” and the company used that to “meet our commitment to the supply of the Northern Territory gas market during the quarter” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

Q&A

  • Scott Hanold, RBC Capital Markets: asked what changed in drilling and the “pro forma cost”; CEO Abbott cited “the bit design,” “the vibration damper,” and said the “directional plans… the way we attack that Moroak Sandstone” helped, adding “in that last well, we got through it with one bit, which was a big win for us,” while emphasizing cost-down needs “repeatability” and “scale across the basin” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • Hanold, RBC Capital Markets: asked about early production/pressure and choke strategy; Abbott said “it's been variable,” “the wells look good… in line with our expectations,” but Tamboran is constrained by “that 25-terajoule a day nomination limitation,” and “we're really interested to see… the long-term decline rates” because “we haven't produced a well out here for more than 90 days” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • Leo Mariani, ROTH: asked about expected near-term CapEx and partner timing; Abbott said capital is focused on “derisking,” cited planned activity across “4 wells in the Pilot Area,” “the 2 Santos wells,” and “the 4 wells in the BCDA,” but said “the full capital program isn't going to be fully locked-in until we finalize who our partner is,” and on timing added, “please bear with us… deals like these take time” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • Jeffrey Grampp, Northland: asked about expanding in-basin sand use and scalability; Abbott said Tamboran is “highly confident in our ability to pump it,” early tracers “look identical,” but “we won't move to a full Red Sand program until we are confident in it,” adding that once proven he could see “a 100% full program of Red Sand” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • Grampp, Northland: asked what milestones matter for potential SPCF expansion; Abbott said the key uncertainty is “making sure that the surrounding infrastructure network will allow us to move the incremental volumes to the incremental markets,” noting “we don't own the pipelines all around us” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • Charles Meade, Johnson Rice: pressed on timing from “25 terajoules” to “40”; Abbott said nominations should rise seasonally and reiterated, “the 25 terajoules a day is a Northern Territory Government limitation,” adding he expects by “the end of the year” to see the “40 terajoule a day target,” while Tamboran will “prioritize at least 2 wells” for long-term decline data (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • Meade, Johnson Rice: asked about Eastern depocenter targets and Tanumbirini history; Abbott said “the primary target is the B shale,” but on older testing added, “I need to go back and check on that,” while CFO Dyer referenced a “vertical frac” and said “there's a lot of prospectivity there” but emphasized limited data history (Chief Executive Officer Abbott; Chief Financial Officer Dyer).

  • Paul Diamond, Citi: asked for “hurdle rate” for moving to 100% local sand and drilling-day targets; Abbott said the key test is whether Red Sand stages “hold up on a relative contribution basis over time,” and on timing targets added, “I think 25 days is a very realistic number for us,” with “more ambitious targets than 25 days” possible “longer term” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • Anish Kapadia, Hannam & Partners: asked what converts pipeline non-binding discussions to binding GSAs and the East Coast pipeline timeline; Abbott said APA has progressed permitting/right-of-way work, but “there's nothing binding that's going to happen until you have a very clear resource,” and he positioned “production data… from the Pilot Area” as “the biggest piece of information to derisk the subsurface” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly positive and catalyst-focused, with repeated drilling/cost and commercialization gating questions; Hanold opened with “Congrats on all the milestones,” while multiple analysts pressed for timelines on nominations, partner process, sand adoption, and pipelines (Scott Hanold, RBC Capital Markets: “Congrats on all the milestones… plenty ahead”).

  • Management’s tone was confident on execution milestones but cautious on timing and subsurface validation; Abbott repeatedly emphasized uncertainty around “long-term decline rates,” saying “we're really interested to see” the declines and “won't know that for a bit,” and he asked investors to “please bear with us” on partnership timing (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • Compared with Q3 fiscal 2026, the current quarter carried more operational proof-points and more near-term commercial mechanics; Q3 centered on “first gas on track,” while Q4 shifted to “First Gas Sales,” commissioning price (“75% of the gas price”), and take-or-pay transition, alongside continued requests for production history (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • The major operational change was moving from planning to delivery; in Q3 Abbott said “first gas on track for the third quarter of this calendar year,” while in Q4 he said, “We have delivered First Gas Sales” and “Gas has now been flowing… for 20 days” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • Funding and liquidity messaging shifted from a larger pro forma figure to reported quarter-end cash; Q3 disclosed “USD 95 million in cash” and “pro forma… USD 298 million,” while Q4 disclosed “USD 225 million in cash” and “pro forma… USD 240 million,” with both quarters noting the same “USD 15 million” receipt expectation subject to conditions (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • Strategic emphasis evolved from farm-out/Falcon process in Q3 to partner discussions plus appraisal cadence in Q4; Q3 noted the Falcon acquisition “anticipated to close,” while Q4 focused on “multiple parties to bring in a strategic partner” and “at least 6 step-out wells over the next 18 months” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • Analyst focus remained consistent on costs, pacing, and commercialization, but Q4 questions concentrated more on decline curves, nominations, and infrastructure gating for expansion decisions, reflecting the start of flowing production (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

Risks and Concerns

  • Abbott highlighted near-term revenue sensitivity to demand nominations and commissioning terms, saying volumes are “limited by market demand” with “25 terajoule per day” nominations and that the company receives “75% of the gas price” during commissioning (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • The company repeatedly flagged the need for longer-run well performance validation: Abbott said the key unknown is “the long-term decline rates” and that the “true test will be the longer-term flow rates and recoveries” for Red Sand stages (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

  • Infrastructure dependency was described as a gating risk for expansion and for pipeline commercialization; Abbott said SPCF expansion depends on certainty that “the surrounding infrastructure network will allow us to move the incremental volumes,” and binding GSAs depend on “a very clear resource” (Chief Executive Officer Abbott).

Final Takeaway

Management said fiscal Q4 marked the shift from pre-first-gas execution to operating commissioning, with Abbott stating the company “delivered First Gas Sales,” is operating under “25 terajoule per day” nominations during commissioning while targeting take-or-pay “40-terajoule per day” supply, and is prioritizing production histories to establish decline curves. Abbott tied the next phase to derisking through “at least 6 step-out wells over the next 18 months,” potential $4 million-per-well completion savings from in-basin sand if longer-term performance holds, and progressing strategic partner discussions while acknowledging that infrastructure certainty and sustained well performance data remain central gating items.

Read the full Earnings Call Transcript

data.title: U.S. airlines offer flight flexibility ahead of Northeast nor’easter
data.description:
Major U.S. airlines are waiving certain change fees and fare differences for eligible travelers as a nor’easter threatens to disrupt weekend travel across the Northeast.

United Airlines (UAL), American Airlines (AAL), and JetBlue Airways (JBLU) issued travel waivers covering flights from Friday through Sunday at airports including New York's John F. Kennedy International, LaGuardia, and Newark Liberty, as well as Boston Logan International.

The storm is expected to bring heavy rain, strong winds, and coastal flooding from North Carolina through New England. Forecasters have warned of wind gusts of up to 60 miles per hour, flooding, and possible power outages, with coastal New England facing some of the strongest conditions.

United's (UAL) waiver covers 10 airports from Philadelphia to Portland, Maine. Eligible passengers traveling September 25 to 27 can move their flights through September 29 without a fare difference, provided they remain in the same cabin and keep the same cities on their itinerary.

American's (AAL) waiver applies to 16 airports, including Philadelphia, Washington, and the three major New York-area airports. Eligible travelers can move trips through September 27 to September 29.

JetBlue's (JBLU) waiver covers 11 airports and allows eligible passengers to rebook through September 30 without change fees or fare differences. Passengers whose flights are canceled can request refunds.

As of Friday morning, delays and cancellations remained limited as airlines continued to assess the storm's path.

data.title: Cognition to hit $1B annualized revenue: report
data.description:
Cognition is on track to reach $1B in annualized revenue this month, roughly doubling its run rate from about four months ago, Bloomberg reported, citing a person familiar with the matter.

The AI coding startup's annualized revenue run rate topped $900M in September, up from $492M in May. The growth has been driven by demand for its Devin AI coding software.

Cognition raised $2B at in a Series E funding round lifting its valuation to $48B from $26B about three months earlier.

The company is among a growing group of AI firms targeting software development. Its customers include Nvidia (NVDA), Citigroup (C), and Mercedes-Benz.

SpaceX  previously approached Cognition about a potential acquisition. SpaceX (SPCX) completed its $60B acquisition of AI coding startup Cursor in August.

A report said Chinese AI startup DeepSeek's (DEEPSEEK) annualized revenue run rate topped $1B. The report put DeepSeek ahead of MiniMax's $800M and roughly in line with Moonshot's $1B run rate.

Z.ai's latest annualized revenue run rate was $1.8B, according to a CNBC transcript. Rhodium estimates annualized revenue of $4B for ByteDance and $2.4B for Alibaba, while OpenAI (OPENAI) and Anthropic (ANTHRO) have reported or been estimated at substantially higher run rates, up to $65B.

data.title: Bill Ackman: ‘The Fed might have just made a mistake. Am I right or am I wrong?’
data.description:
Bill Ackman, CEO of Pershing Square, is questioning whether the Federal Reserve’s traditional approach to fighting inflation remains effective amid an unprecedented surge in demand for artificial intelligence and energy.

“The presumption that the Fed raising short-term rates reduces inflation is predicated on the belief that higher rates reduce demand and investment,” Ackman stated. 

However, Ackman argued that assumption may not hold in the current economic environment, where demand for computing power and energy could remain strong regardless of borrowing costs. 

“What if higher rates don’t reduce demand and investment because the demand for intelligence and energy is unaffected by higher rates?” he asked, citing the potentially enormous returns associated with winning the race for advanced AI. 

Ackman also warned that higher interest costs could become embedded throughout the economy, potentially creating additional inflationary pressure. 

“The problem is compounded as the more the Fed raises rates, the more inflation we will have,” he said, suggesting policymakers could face a cycle in which additional tightening generates further price pressures. 

Ackman ultimately questioned whether conventional economic models apply to the current environment, adding, “I think the Fed might have just made a mistake. Am I right or am I wrong?”
